newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German spymaster Wolf denied U.S. entry.
newsitem.headline: East German spymaster Wolf denied U.S. entry.

text.p: The United States will not lift an entry ban on former East German spymaster Markus Wolf to allow him to publicise his autobiography there, a spokesman for the U.S. embassy in Bonn said on Tuesday.
Wolf's three decades as head of Communist East Germany's foreign intelligence service made him an opponent both of the former West Germany and of the United States, the spokesman said.
"We do not think it is appropriate to give him a waiver (from the ban)," the spokesman said, quoting directly from comments made by U.S. State Department in Washington on Monday.
Last month a German court gave Wolf a two-year suspended sentence after convicting him of Cold War crimes including kidnapping, coercion and bodily harm.

Wolf's autobiography, "Man Without a Face" was launched in 14 countries and 11 languages last Monday with a picture of the 74-year-old staring out from the cover with a steely gaze. The U.S. publisher is Random House.

In his book, Wolf said that a former director of the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency tried to recruit him at the end of the Cold War by offering him a house, a small fortune and a new identity in California in exchange for information about agents operating in the United States.
